_comment: Verifies reaction_diffusion pitfall 6 on scikit-fem 12.0.1 (2026-08-06). The natural half is pinned on pure diffusion where the answer is known: with no boundary treatment at all the total mass 1^T M u is conserved to a relative -1.2e-15 over 50 steps; with the boundary DOFs condensed to 0, 70.1% of the mass drains. The Schnakenberg half (16x16 ElementQuad1, 289 DOFs, 64 boundary DOFs, dt=2e-3, 20 steps): natural Neumann gives u on the boundary in [0.118, 4.35] and spread 4.23, while condense(J, -R, D=boundary) gives boundary values identically 0, the whole field inside [0, 0.125] and spread 0.125 - a 34x amplitude suppression, so the constraint does not merely flatten the boundary, it suppresses the pattern. API note recorded by the fixture: scikit-fem 12.0.1 has NO DirichletBC symbol; the essential-BC API is condense / enforce / penalize, so the claim's wording is borrowed from another library.
